method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Compilation incorporating amendments up to the Community Titles Act 2018 (No. 32 of 2018, in operation 30 June 2021), last reprint Reprint 3 as at 22 May 2015, as deposited at registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_43948.txt (retrieved 7 September 2026); no regulations used; local laws prescribing a sufficient fence not deposited, taken as inputs

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: From the seat of the neighbouring owner: who is an owner (s 5), what is a sufficient fence as far as the Act states, with the local law as an input (s 5), the equal share of a new fence and the effect of an agreement or the Crown (ss 4, 6(1), 7), the notice to fence and how it is given (ss 8, 22(1)-(2)), when either owner may apply to the Magistrates Court (s 9(1)), building the whole fence on default and recovering half (s 10), the claim for half the value of a fence built without notice and the one month to pay or dispute (s 13(1)-(4), (7)), repairs: equal shares, the repair notice and 14-day reply, urgent repairs, fire or tree damage through one owner's neglect (ss 14, 15(1)-(4), (7), (8)), landlord and tenant shares (s 19(1)), entry to build or repair (s 21). Community titles, absent owners, surveys, road-boundary fences, the court's orders and costs, and machinery out.
lives: chloe c07b (2039-08-15): a dividing fence with the new neighbour -- who pays for it? half each (s 7)
